title: St Valentine's and St Dwynwen's Days
when_text: 14 February; in Wales St Dwynwen's Day, 25 January, is kept as well or instead
intro: St Valentine was a Roman martyr with no known link to love until English poets of the 1380s tied his feast to birds choosing their mates. Love letters, verses and then cheap printed cards followed, and Victorian penny postage turned it into a festival of the post. Wales has its own saint of lovers, Dwynwen, whose ruined church stands on a tidal island off Anglesey.

facts.title: Chaucer's birds choose their mates
facts.text: The first known link between St Valentine's Day and romantic love is in Geoffrey Chaucer's Parlement of Foules, a dream poem in which birds gather on the saint's day to choose their mates. It is usually dated to about 1381-82.

sources.title: Valentine's Day (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: The first recorded association of Saint Valentine's Day with romantic love is believed to be in the Parliament of Fowls (1382) by Geoffrey Chaucer, a dream vision portraying a parliament for birds to choose their mates.

sources.title: Parlement of Foules (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: there is nowadays a general agreement among scholars as to 1381–1382 being the date of composition

facts.title: No Roman love festival behind it
facts.text: The often repeated idea that Valentine's Day carries on the Roman Lupercalia has no evidence behind it: it was first put forward by antiquarians in the 18th century, and the saint's day had no romantic meaning before Chaucer's time.

sources.title: Valentine's Day (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: with a connection to the Lupercalia first asserted in 18th century antiquarian works

sources.title: Valentine's Day (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: The celebration of Saint Valentine is not known to have had any romantic connotations until Chaucer's poetry

facts.title: A valentine from a prisoner in the Tower
facts.text: The earliest surviving valentine is a French rondeau by Charles, Duke of Orléans, to his wife, written while he was a prisoner in the Tower of London after his capture at Agincourt in 1415.

sources.title: Valentine's Day (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: At the time, the duke was being held in the Tower of London following his capture at the Battle of Agincourt, 1415.

facts.title: "My right well-beloved Valentine"
facts.text: The earliest surviving valentines in English were written in 1477 by Margery Brews of Norfolk to John Paston, whom she was to marry. They are among the Paston Letters, most of which are now in the British Library.

sources.title: Valentine's Day (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: The earliest surviving valentines in English appear to be those in the Paston Letters, written in 1477 by Margery Brews to her future husband John Paston "my right well-beloved Valentine".

sources.title: Paston Letters (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: Most of the Paston letters and associated documents are now in the British Library

facts.title: Ophelia's valentine song
facts.text: Shakespeare gave the day a sad turn in Hamlet, where Ophelia sings of being a maid at a window on St Valentine's morning.

sources.title: Valentine's Day (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: Saint Valentine's Day is mentioned ruefully by Ophelia in William Shakespeare's Hamlet (1600–1601)

facts.title: Verses for the tongue-tied
facts.text: In 1797 a British publisher brought out The Young Man's Valentine Writer, a book of ready-made sentimental verses for suitors who could not write their own.

sources.title: Valentine's Day (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: In 1797, a British publisher issued The Young Man's Valentine Writer, which contained scores of suggested sentimental verses for the young lover unable to compose his own.

facts.title: The penny post and the valentine boom
facts.text: Some 60,000 valentines went through the post in 1835, when postage was dear. After Rowland Hill's reforms and the Penny Black of 1840 the number rose to 400,000 within a year.

sources.title: Valentine's Day (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: In 1835, 60,000 Valentine cards were sent by post in the United Kingdom, despite postage being expensive.

sources.title: Valentine's Day (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: with 400,000 sent just one year after its introduction

facts.title: Jack Valentine in Norfolk
facts.text: In Norfolk a figure called Jack Valentine knocks at the back door of houses and leaves sweets and presents for the children.

sources.title: Valentine's Day (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: In Norfolk, a character called "Jack" Valentine knocks on the rear door of houses, leaving sweets and presents for children.

facts.title: A saint's bones sent to Dublin
facts.text: In 1835 Rome sent part of the remains said to be St Valentine's, with a small vessel said to hold his blood, to the Carmelite friar John Spratt in Dublin. They are in Whitefriar Street Church, where people come on the day to pray for love.

sources.title: Saint Valentine (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: On 27 December 1835, the Very Reverend Father John Spratt, Master of Sacred Theology to the Carmelite order in Dublin, was sent the partial remains of St Valentine by Cardinal Carlo Odescalchi

sources.title: Saint Valentine (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: they pray at the shrine in hope of finding romance

facts.title: Dwynwen and Maelon
facts.text: In one version of her story Dwynwen, a daughter of King Brychan, turned away a young man called Maelon and prayed to be free of her love for him; an angel's potion froze him to ice. Granted three wishes, she asked that he be thawed, that God watch over all true lovers, and that she never marry.

sources.title: Saint Dwynwen (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: An angel appears with a potion: Maelon turns to ice.

sources.title: Saint Dwynwen (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: that God, through Dwynwen, watch over all true lovers; and that she herself remain unmarried

facts.title: Wales's own day for lovers
facts.text: Calendars from the 15th century give Dwynwen's feast as 25 January. Revived as a lovers' day in modern times, it was well established by 2004, and many in Wales now keep it instead of or as well as 14 February.

sources.title: Saint Dwynwen (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: Calendars from the fifteenth century and later assign her feast day to 25 January.

sources.title: Saint Dwynwen (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: by 2004, the celebration of 25 January as a feast for Welsh lovers was well established

facts.title: Fish that told lovers' fortunes
facts.text: Dwynwen's holy well on Llanddwyn Island drew medieval pilgrims, who watched the sacred fish in its water to learn whether their love would prosper.

sources.title: Saint Dwynwen (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: A holy well on the island, associated with Dwynwen, became a site of pilgrimage, where the movements of sacred fish within its waters were thought to forecast lovers' fortunes.

facts.title: The oldest Welsh lovespoon
facts.text: Carved wooden lovespoons are a Welsh love token. The oldest known Welsh lovespoon, dated 1667, is at St Fagans National Museum of History, which holds more than 300 of them.

where.name: St Fagans National Museum of History

sources.title: Lovespoon (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: The second is a true Welsh lovespoon, and is part of the collection at the St Fagans National History Museum in Wales. dated to 1667

sources.title: Lovespoon (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: the St Fagans National History Museum holding more than 300 spoons

places.name: Whitefriar Street Carmelite Church
places.why: Dublin church holding relics said to be St Valentine's, sent from Rome in 1835; a place of pilgrimage on 14 February for people hoping to find love.

sources.title: Saint Valentine (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: Other relics of him are in Whitefriar Street Carmelite Church, Dublin, Ireland, a popular place of pilgrimage, especially on Saint Valentine's Day, for those seeking love.

places.name: Blessed John Duns Scotus Church, Gorbals
places.why: Glasgow church said to hold relics of St Valentine.

sources.title: Saint Valentine (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: Alleged relics of St. Valentine also lie at the reliquary of Roquemaure, Gard, France, in the St. Stephen's Cathedral, Vienna, in Balzan in Malta and also in Blessed John Duns Scotus Church in the Gorbals area of Glasgow, Scotland.

places.name: Ynys Llanddwyn
places.why: Tidal island off Anglesey where Dwynwen is said to have lived as a hermit until about AD 460; her holy well here was visited by lovers.

sources.title: Saint Dwynwen (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: she retreats to the solitude of Ynys Llanddwyn off Anglesey, becoming a hermit until her death around AD 460

places.name: St Dwynwen's Church, Llanddwyn
places.why: Ruins of the church named after Dwynwen, a major shrine in the Middle Ages; digs in 2011 and 2021 found traces of older buildings beneath.

sources.title: Saint Dwynwen (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: St Dwynwen's Church on Ynys Llanddwyn evolved into a major shrine during the Middle Ages.

sources.title: Llanddwyn (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: The 2021 dig discovered traces of even older buildings below the ruins.

places.name: St Adwenna's Church, Advent
places.why: Grade I listed 15th-century church in Cornwall dedicated to St Adwen, a daughter of King Brychan who is often confused with Dwynwen.

sources.title: Advent, Cornwall (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: The Grade I listed parish church is dedicated to St Adwen, one of the daughters of King Brychan of Brycheiniog, often conflated with St Dwynwen, the patron saint of Love.

places.name: Westminster Abbey
places.why: Burial place of Geoffrey Chaucer, the poet who first tied St Valentine's Day to love; he was the first writer buried in what became Poets' Corner.

sources.title: Geoffrey Chaucer (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: He was the first writer to be buried in what has since become Poets' Corner in Westminster Abbey.

places.name: Tower of London
places.why: Where Charles, Duke of Orléans, was held after Agincourt when he wrote the earliest surviving valentine.

sources.title: Valentine's Day (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: At the time, the duke was being held in the Tower of London following his capture at the Battle of Agincourt, 1415.

places.name: British Library
places.why: Holds most of the Paston Letters, among them Margery Brews's valentines of 1477, the oldest in English.

sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.quote: Margery Brews' famous Valentines to John Paston III
